title: A new frontier of app monetization: spatial paywalls.
summary: With Apple Vision Pro out in the wild, we begin to wonder — what does app monetization look like now?
body_text: Spatial Paywalls: What does monetization look like in visionOS? Now that visionOS is out in the wild, there seems to be one of those magical Apple moments happening: technology before this moment, and technology afterwards. Sure, when the iPhone launched, there were scores of existing devices to choose from. But the iPhone was so different, so advanced and so forward thinking — it changed mobile phones for good. With Apple Vision Pro, I'd wager the same thing will happen in the AR/VR space. Technologies like passthrough, high fidelity displays and hand tracking have been around a while now. But, Apple Vision Pro is doing those things better than what's come before. And, it's attempting its own "wrinkles" in the space — think digital personas, immersive environments and most importantly, visionOS itself. So, will the marquee features of visionOS and mixed reality environments impact monetization strategies? If what's here and what's to come is new and different — does that mean app monetization will be different, too? Does the design of our paywalls change? How can we present information differently in this new space? That's a question all of us at Superwall have been asking ourselves since February 2nd. In fact, we think it's such an important point to consider that we ended up buying everyone on the team their own Apple Vision Pro. As we've been using it more, here are the questions we've been trying to find answers to: What's new about visionOS design now? What do we know, and how does it relate to paywalls? Will developers leverage ARKit, RealityKit, and other visionOS frameworks to create value-added features or content specific to the device? And will those be core to the upsell experience? What will the best practices be? We don't have the answers quite yet, but I think we'd all have to start with the first one. visionOS' design language The first thing Apple says when you visit their design documentation is that people enter an "infinite 3D space" when using Apple Vision Pro. visionOS Design Header Already, that changes everything . In comparison to the input models we're used to, you can interact with software in a full, 3D space now. Tapping a flat, rectangular screen is a world apart from tapping your finger together as a "click", or moving your eyes around as a mouse. The depth, immersion and nascent input models meant there was a novel opportunity for Apple to make a new operating system (which they did!). Even though visionOS was based off of iPadOS, you can feel the new design language immediately. Check out Notes here on visionOS — you can feel that its Notes by looking at it. The view hierarchy is nearly the same, but yet it feels much different than it does on iPadOS or macOS. Messages in visionOS Notes macOS Sonoma Cliché as it may be, they are the same yet different. So, what does that mean for paywalls? Do we simply remove opaque backgrounds, add in the glass effect and ensure we're using the native controls? That's what I did for my own app, though I'm not convinced that it's doing visionOS justice. It simply is visionOS enough right now. Will "spatial" paywalls become an emerging concept? Paywalls that take advantage of Spatial Audio, immersion and spatial input? Or, will the simple windowed interfaces continue to work? Perhaps it will be a mix of the two, sort of like how visionOS apps appear today? There seems to be an opportunity here to take advantage of the new APIs and technology of Vision Pro and do better that what's out there. Elite Hoops iPadOS Paywall Elite Hoops visionOS Paywall Locked Notes: Access visionOS Paywall Final Thoughts It's an exciting time to be developing for Apple's platforms. It's no secret our goal is to help developers ultimately make money to sustain their business' with our configurable and testable paywalls. And that mission is why Apple Vision Pro is so fun for us to think about — we simply don't know how to best monetize here yet! The things we're doing today? They'll probably look elementary in five years from now. The designs, interaction models and overall flows. But, we're happy to be on the journey with you as we figure all of this out. Be sure to keep an eye out for some new things we're already workshopping here at Superwall specifically for Apple Vision Pro. We're investing in the platform, and we can't wait to help developers monetize in visionOS.

title: Days of Thunder Sequel Gets Green Light
summary: Tom Cruise will soon be back on track as Cole Trickle, as the much-anticipated Days of Thunder 2 has been given the go-ahead by Paramount Pictures. The Hollywood Reporter claims that Jonathan Levine will direct the sequel to the 1990 NASCAR movie, fresh from steering the upcoming NFL drama Mr. Irrelevant. Sundance Award-winning Levine’s back […]
body_text: Tom Cruise will soon be back on track as Cole Trickle, as the much-anticipated Days of Thunder 2 has been given the go-ahead by Paramount Pictures. The Hollywood Reporter claims that Jonathan Levine will direct the sequel to the 1990 NASCAR movie, fresh from steering the upcoming NFL drama Mr. Irrelevant . Sundance Award-winning Levine’s back catalog swerves between horror, comedy, and more serious cinema. He also worked with Cruise’s former Thunder co-star (and ex-wife) Nicole Kidman on Hulu’s Nine Perfect Strangers . Beyond Cruise himself, no other cast members have been confirmed, so we don’t know whether Cary Elwes will reappear as Trickle’s rival Russ Wheeler or if Randy Quaid will be back as team owner Tim Daland. Sadly, Robert Duvall, who played ace mechanic and pit boss Harry Hogge, passed away this year. Expect an emotional tribute in the storyline somewhere and a repeat of the immortal words, “Rubbin’ is racing.” The script has been handed over to Will Staples, who made his name writing for video games such as Call of Duty 3: Modern Warfare, before acting as co-writer on the 2021 action movie Without Remorse , starring Michael B. Jordan. The original Days of Thunder paired Cruise with Top Gun director Tony Scott and took almost $158 million at the box office. 2022’s Top Gun: Maverick , meanwhile, achieved more than $1.5 billion globally, suggesting that, even over 30 years later, there’s still no stopping the Cruise missile at the movies. Production is expected to begin in 2027, giving Cruise, once Top Gear ‘s fastest Star in a Reasonably Priced Car, plenty of time to brush up on his driving skills and make sure he’s got a set of tires that are “matched perfect and staggered special.” The post Days of Thunder Sequel Gets Green Light appeared first on Hagerty Media .

title: How Solarflare built a real-time selfie experience for Hennessy's Hip Hop 50
summary: Solarflare integrated Photoroom's Background Remover API to build a real-time selfie generator for Hennessy's Hip Hop 50 campaign across live events. See how.
body_text: Solarflare Studio used Photoroom's Background Remover API to build a real-time selfie generator for Hennessy's Hip Hop 50th anniversary campaign. The tool removed backgrounds from fan selfies on the spot and placed them into era-themed Hip Hop portrait templates, creating shareable content at multi-city live events where guests got results in seconds. Life before Photoroom No real-time tool for live background removal at events Fan portrait creation required manual editing after the fact Limited options for instant, shareable branded content on-site Life with Photoroom Real-time background removal at live events via the API Fans received personalized portraits in seconds Shareable, era-themed content generated on the spot across cities "Implementing Photoroom's Background Remover API was a very straightforward process, which is exactly what we look for in our tools. By seamlessly merging the capabilities of their AI-driven photo editing software into our social-first digital experience, our project is consistently producing top-notch results." — John Martinelli, Head of Production, Solarflare Integrate Photoroom’s API to run global fan campaigns When Hennessy released a limited edition VS bottle to mark Hip Hop's 50th anniversary, the brand wanted more than a product launch. They wanted fans to feel like part of the celebration. Laundry Service, Hennessy's partner agency, brought in Solarflare Studio , a creative technology agency based in London, to make that happen. Solarflare's concept was called "Rep Yours": a selfie-based portrait generator that let fans pick their favorite Hip Hop era and coast, then see themselves transported into a custom visual from that moment in the culture's history. The portraits were designed to be shared instantly on social media, extending the campaign's reach beyond the room. The idea was ambitious. But making it work at a live event, where guests are standing in front of a screen expecting an instant result, introduced a problem that most digital campaigns never have to solve. Creating instant portraits at a live event with no room for error At a live brand activation, the margin for failure is zero. A guest takes a selfie, and the system needs to remove the background, composite the portrait into a themed template, and return a finished image, all within seconds. If the cutout is rough, the portrait looks wrong. If the system is slow, the line backs up. Either way, the experience falls apart in front of the person waiting for it. Solarflare needed a background removal solution that could process real-time selfies with enough accuracy to produce shareable, high-quality portraits on the spot. The tool also had to run reliably across multiple live events in different cities, with no downtime during the campaign. The API solution that worked on the first try Solarflare assessed multiple background removal solutions before choosing Photoroom's Background Remover API . The deciding factor was trust: the team had seen the technology used across similar live experiences and validated it as a tried-and-tested solution before committing. Here's how the selfie generator worked after Solarflare integrated the Photoroom API: A fan stepped up to the activation, took or uploaded a selfie, and the system sent the image to Photoroom's API. The API removed the background in real time and placed the cutout into one of several era-themed Hip Hop portrait templates. The fan then received the finished image within seconds, ready to download and share on social media. This process ran in multiple cities where Hennessy hosted events for their anniversary. Selfie portraits from Hennessy’s activation campaign. Source: Solarflare Studio The result: reliable performance across a multi-city live campaign After launching the Hennessy Hip Hop 50 selfie generator with Photoroom's API integration, Wolt achieved: No technical failures across all live events, with the API processing selfies in real time. Instant fan portraits generated on the spot, with background removal accurate enough for guests to share directly on social media. Multi-city deployment with the same workflow running reliably across different events and locations. The agency now considers Photoroom a standing part of its experiential technology stack for future entertainment campaigns . "Photoroom's reliability makes it a welcome addition to our experiential toolkit, and we're excited about our ongoing partnership." — John Martinelli, Head of Production, Solarflare Photoroom processes millions of images for agencies and developers creating fan-centered visual campaigns at scale, such as Hennessy’s Rep Yours for Hip Hop 50 and Warner Bros. Barbie movie campaign . Solarflare's work demonstrates that the same API handling millions of product listings daily is fast and reliable enough for consumer-facing experiences where guests watch the result appear in real time.

title: S&P Global to Acquire datacenterHawk Connecting Global Data Center, Power and Infrastructure Markets
summary: Unites S&P Global Energy data center, infrastructure and power markets data & insights with datacenterHawk's asset-level intelligence to create a comprehensive and industry-leading platform for...
body_text: Unites S&P Global Energy data center, infrastructure and power markets data & insights with datacenterHawk's asset-level intelligence to create a comprehensive and industry-leading platform for critical infrastructure and energy expansion NEW YORK , July 28, 2026 / PRNewswire / -- S&P Global (NYSE: SPGI) today announced it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire datacenterHawk, a leading provider of proprietary intelligence for the global data center, fiber optic and related infrastructure markets. The acquisition will bring together leading data center forecasting, market outlooks and technology intelligence from 451 Research, part of S&P Global Energy, alongside comprehensive coverage of global power markets across grid infrastructure and intelligence, and supply/demand forecasts, with datacenterHawk's proprietary asset-level intelligence on data center supply/demand, pricing, pipelines and site selection, as well as its Fiber Locator platform. The transaction underscores S&P Global's commitment to customers who are investors and operators of AI infrastructure through providing advanced Essential Intelligence – the data, expertise and connected technology that enable governments, businesses, investors, and individuals to make decisions with conviction. By combining proprietary asset-level data with advanced analytics and AI-ready insights, S&P Global Energy expects to empower customers with greater transparency into one of the fastest-growing areas of global infrastructure. Customers will have access to a clearer view of operational and planned data centers, where capacity is emerging and how AI infrastructure growth is reshaping demand for power, compute, connectivity, land, supply chains and sustainable infrastructure. "AI is transforming not only technology markets, but the physical infrastructure and energy systems that underpin the global economy, with significant implications for productivity, investment and GDP growth," said Dave Ernsberger, President of S&P Global Energy . "By bringing datacenterHawk into S&P Global Energy, we are reinforcing our energy expansion strategy, helping our customers make real-time decisions with confidence in one of the most important infrastructure markets of the next decade." Upon close, the acquisition is expected to strengthen S&P Global Energy's ability to connect data center intelligence with power, renewables, sustainability, critical materials, supply chain and energy transition data, while supporting new benchmarks, indices and analytics that bring greater transparency to compute demand, data center capacity, pricing and infrastructure availability. "The data center market has become a critical intersection point for AI, energy, capital investment and sustainability," said David Liggitt, Founder and CEO of datacenterHawk . "Customers need intelligence that connects critical infrastructure growth with power markets, grid constraints, supply chains and environmental considerations. By combining 451 Research and datacenterHawk, we expect to give customers a more complete view of where capacity, investment and demand are likely to emerge." The transaction is expected to close in 2H 2026, subject to customary closing conditions. The acquisition is not expected to have a material impact on the financial results of S&P Global or the S&P Global Energy division. We are Advancing Essential Intelligence through world-leading benchmarks, data, and insights that customers need in order to plan confidently, act decisively and thrive in a rapidly changing global landscape. From helping our customers assess new investments across the capital and commodities markets to navigating the energy expansion, acceleration of artificial intelligence, and evolution of public and private markets, we enable the world's leading organizations to unlock opportunities, solve challenges and plan for tomorrow – today. Learn more at www.spglobal.com . About S&P Global Energy At S&P Global Energy, our comprehensive view of global energy and commodities markets enables our customers to make superior decisions and create long-term, sustainable value. Our four core capabilities are: Platts for pricing and news; CERA for research and advisory; Horizons for energy expansion and sustainability solutions; and Events for industry collaboration.
